newsitem.title: USA: US West unit's debt tightens in secondary market.
newsitem.headline: US West unit's debt tightens in secondary market.

text.p: All six issues of US West Capital Funding's $4.1 billion debt offering tightened in the secondary market an indication dealers said of the tremendous demand for the paper.
"The demand has been incredible," said one syndicate source. "All issues have tightend in the secondary market."
US West Capital's, a unit of US West Inc, $4.1 billion debt offering which was successfully priced on Thursday became the largest investment grade deal ever in U.S. corporate bond history.
-7.95 percent 100-year bonds were 115 bid, 112 offer, following its pricing at 120 basis points over Treasuries.
-8.15 percent 35-year bonds were seen at 130 bid, after pricing at a spread of 132 basis points over Treasuries.

Merrill Lynch said the deal was upped in size three times in efforts to meet growing demand from its initially planned four-part $2.0 billion debt offering and two additional tranches, 35-year and 100-year, were added.
According to US West Inc Treasurer James Anderson the $200 million 35-year tranche, with a 10-year call feature, was placed with a single large institutional investor.
Lead underwriter for the deal, Merrill Lynch & Co, said on Thursday, the deal was substantially oversubscribed going into the pricing and could have easily been priced in excess of $5.0 billion.
All of US West Capital Funding's six issues were trading at a tighter spread in the secondary market, an indication of how great demand was for the paper and continues to be, dealers said on Friday.
The following is a breakdown of US West Capital's six issues:
-6.85 percent five-year notes, which were priced at 55 basis points over Treasuries are currently trading at a 52 bid, 50 offer
-7.30 percent 10-year notes were seen at 78 bid, 75 offer, after pricing at a spread of 80 basis points over Treasuries.
-7.90 percent 30-year bond were 102 bid, 99 offer, following its pricing at 107 basis points over Treasuries.
-6.95 percent 40-year bonds, put seven, were 54 bid, tightening after pricing at a spread of 56 basis points.
The underwriter said the 10- and 30-year issues were the most heavily oversubscribed issues in the offering.
Turning to other issues, American Health Properties today priced a two-part $220 million Baa3/BBB-minus rated debt offering via lead manager Goldman Sachs & Co.
The $100 million 7.05 percent five-year notes were priced to yield 80 basis points over Treasuries.
The $120 million 7.50 percent 10-year notes were priced to yield 105 basis points over Treasuries.
Corporate bond activity is expected to wind down early today as players head home ahead of Monday's Martin Luther King holiday.
PSA The Bond Market Trade Association recommended an early 1400 EST/1900 GMT close for the U.S. credit market and a full close on Monday for the holiday.
((-- Nancy Leinfuss, 212-859-1675 ))
